text:
The Flames are 9-11-1 with 19 points, and the season has a hole in it now: Kevin Bahl is out for the year, and he was half of Calgary's most-used pairing with Simon Nemec. The headlines since have been about who replaces him, and the AHL depth chart is being tested.

The bigger issue is scoring. Calgary has 51 goals in 21 games, 2.43 a night, and that's seven fewer than its chances deserve. The chances aren't great either: 45% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) overall and 46% at five on five. The power play is the quietest in this group, 0.37 expected goals a game, and the Flames take more penalties (4.0 a night) than they draw. None of the top three lines is winning its minutes; Morgan Frost's line with Yegor Sharangovich and Aydar Suniev, at 49%, comes closest.

There are bright spots. Zayne Parekh is breaking out and running the power play, and Dustin Wolf's win in Los Angeles was a reminder he can steal a night. Devin Cooley has had his moments too, though Sunday's 6-1 loss in Anaheim wasn't one of the better nights in front of him.

Our simulations project about 77 points and a 9% playoff chance. Watch Parekh's minutes and what the front office does about the blue line.
